jobs.description:
Job Description

Director, Enterprise Strategy & Transformation (ES&T), Royal Bank of Canada US, New York, NY:

Perform comprehensive strategic reviews and analyses leveraging frameworks, approaches, tools and methodologies and develop robust recommendations to support Group Executive, segment Operating Committees, and lines of business. Ensure growth strategies are well developed, articulated and aligned across businesses and with enterprise perspective/priorities, and proactively identify benefits such as revenue streams or cost savings opportunities. Support the annual enterprise strategic development process, business portfolio review, and related senior leader off sites/events to advance RBC’s strategy. Produce materials for Group Executive and Board for review, discussion, and decision. Gain the position of trusted advisor and help facilitate trade-off / prioritization decisions with senior leaders, strategists, functions, cross-functional project teams and colleagues by providing rigorous strategic insight based on thorough research and analysis. Lead projects end-to-end exhibiting complete ‘ownership’ of the problem, continuously pushing the thinking, while managing stakeholders, junior team members, timelines, and deliverables. Mentor and coach Senior Managers and Managers on the team on core strategy skills, professional development, and career management.

Telecommuting permitted up to 1 day per week.

#LI-DNI

Full-time employment, Monday – Friday, 40 hours per week, $203,000.00 per year.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

Masters degree in Business administration, Economics, International Development or a related field and 3 years of related work experience.

Must have 3 years experience in:

- Corporate Strategy, Management Consulting, Capital Markets or product management and strategy within the Financial Services, FinTech or technology industry.

- Evaluate, develop, or scale new and emerging businesses, including digital business models, platform-based offerings, or technology-enabled products and services.

- Design, manage, and implement complex, cross-functional projects, including defining scope and objectives, managing timelines and stakeholders, and delivering measurable business outcomes.

- Develop and build complex financial models associated with business cases, Bank P&L and balance sheet multiple lines of business in Capital Markets, Global Asset Management, Personal Banking and Wealth.

- Operating model design, governance and decision rights, organization chart implications, and change management.

- Project design, management and implementation including translating complex problem statements, determining scope and translate them into discrete projects.

- Support the annual enterprise strategic development process, business portfolio review.

The base salary for this job is $203,000.00 per year.  This salary does not include other elements of total compensation, including a discretionary bonus and benefits such as a 401(k) program with company-matching contributions; health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance; and paid time-off plan.

- Drives RBC’s high performance culture

- Enables collective achievement of our strategic goals

- Generates sustainable shareholder returns and above market shareholder value

jobs.title: Director Private Banking
jobs.description:
Job Description

APPLICATION DEADLINE: OCTOBER 30, 2026

What is the opportunity?
The Director Private Banking role is a pivotal leadership opportunity to shape the trajectory of RBC's Ultra High Net Worth business across the Caribbean region. In this role, you will serve as the trusted strategic advisor and relationship steward for a select portfolio of UHNW individuals and families, orchestrating exceptional experiences that deepen client loyalty while navigating the sophisticated financial, regulatory, and reputational complexities inherent to this segment. Beyond portfolio stewardship and profitability optimization, you will drive new client acquisition initiatives and elevate advisory capabilities across the region by mentoring Private Bankers and cultivating best practices in UHNW wealth management. Leading a dynamic Client Relationship Team, you will position RBC as the premier private banking partner by delivering the full breadth of our capabilities—tailored to each client's unique circumstances and aspirations—while upholding the highest standards of fiduciary responsibility and ethical conduct. This role offers the chance to build a high-performing team, expand market presence in a strategically important segment, and make a lasting impact on client outcomes and organizational excellence.

What will you do?
- Deliver exceptional client experience to steer and grow UHNW client relationships within your portfolio of clients providing strategic relationship management and proactive advice to high-net-worth households following all five principles of the Black Card Experience.
- Be an advocate for the client and lead the One RBC Orchestration with RBC partners to bring the full gamut of technical advice from partners within Caribbean Banking and globally internally across RBC businesses and externally with key COIs to win the full client relationship, manage referrals end to end, align businesses to the Home of Best Fit, and ensure credit opportunities are proactively identified and captured by the Senior Manager Credit Structures to align advice with overall client strategy.
- Acquire new relationships by building a strong network in your local market while growing and deepening existing client relationships through discovery and advice, introducing clients to the right solutions, partners, and capabilities at the right time, to help meet client needs both within Private Banking and across RBC.
- Ensure portfolio quality and compliance in close collaboration with the Senior Manager Credit Structures.
- Lead the client relationship team introducing the team members as a key partners, respecting and reinforcing role clarity, to deliver exceptional day-to-day banking services, and as the credit expert for credit advice and solutions to meet the needs of the client household.
- You are a role model, coach and contributing to a culture of winning as One RBC by demonstrating commitment to support leadership and assisting colleagues by sharing expertise within Caribbean Private Banking and to help develop our Private Bankers, strengthen their capabilities, and elevate the overall level of Private Banking proficiency across the region.

What do you need to succeed?
Must-have

- MBA, CFA or equivalent relevant Postgraduate or professional designation
- Minimum 7-10 years’ experience in a sales environment inclusive of at least 5 years at a senior sales leadership level providing advice and solutions to VHNW/UHNW worth clients
- Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
- Thorough understanding of high-net-worth financial sales and client relationship management
- Strong negotiations skills
- Strong leadership skills and a champion for change
- Growth mindset, continuous learner with a deep curiosity about enhancing the client experience, emotionally intelligent, decisive, and excellent judgment
- Strong observational coaching, people development and mentoring skills

Nice to Have:
- Experience in Commercial Financial Services
- Professional designations (e.g. FEA, MBA, LL.B., CFA, CPA)
-  Successful completion of Wealth Management Essential or Certification in Wealth Management (CIWM) designation under Moody’s/Canadian Securities Institute

What’s in it for you?
We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.
- A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits
- Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
- Ability to make a difference and lasting impact
- Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
- Opportunities to do challenging work

What is the opportunity?

Along with portfolio management responsibilities, you collaborate with the Director in various account planning and risk management activities that grow relationships, enhance loyalty and drive innovation.

What will you do?

- Develop portfolio and individual client growth plans and reviews with Managing Director/Director
- Implement client calling strategies and opportunity developing/tiering activities for existing and targeted clients to ensure an exceptional client experience, retain accounts and to grow Cash Management, Deposit and RBC revenue

- Work with and actively engage partners within the enterprise in relation to industry negotiations, changes, and initiatives

jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?
As the Manager of Operations Process Engineering, you will act as a lead and critical contributor to Technology & Enterprise Operations’ (TEO) transformation programs to meet our core goals of enhancing assigned operational domains - Cash Services, Payments & Trade, and Finance Shared Services Operations.

Our team is specifically accountable for conducting comprehensive current state analysis, identifying re-engineering and AI/automation opportunities, developing business cases, and designing future-state processes that result in improvements to efficiency, productivity, digitization, and risk reduction. This pivotal role directly contributes to operational excellence and innovation across the department.

What will you do?
- Process Re-Engineering: - Conduct comprehensive current-state process diagnostics and root cause analysis
- Identify and document re-engineering, automation, and AI opportunities with clear business rationale and impact potential
- Create process maps at varying levels—from end-to-end process flows to granular step-by-step designs—for both current and future state processes

- Opportunity Assessment & Business Case Development: - Evaluate opportunities for AI, GenAI, RPA, and workflow automation for feasibility and scalability
- Support business case development and ROI analysis

- Future State Process Redesign and Transformation Delivery: - Design future-state processes and document detailed process logic, business requirements, and capabilities
- Collaborate in cross-functional redesign, solutioning, and feasibility sessions

- Stakeholder Engagement: - Build effective working relationships with Ops Center SMEs, process owners, IT, Data, and Risk
- Communicate findings and recommendations with clarity; participate in workshops and design sessions to gather requirements and validate solutions
- Identify and escalate risks, dependencies, and compliance considerations to Senior Manager for governance review

What do you need to succeed?
Must Have
- Bachelor's or Master’s Degree in Industrial Engineering, Business, Innovation, Technology Management or related field

- 3+ years of experience in process improvement and IT transformation: - Deep understanding of process design, mapping, value stream analysis, and Lean Six Sigma
- Ability to create clear, comprehensive process documentation, design specifications, and work product documentation to enterprise standards

- Strong communication skills with proven ability to facilitate cross-functional meetings
- Interest in and basic understanding of technologies (Generative AI, Agentic AI, ML, RPA)
- Intermediate proficiency in data analysis to support business case development
- Strong PowerPoint presentation skills
- Self-motivation and ability to thrive in dynamic, fast-paced environments
- Structured problem-solving, curiosity, and critical thinking capabilities

jobs.location: Jersey City, New Jersey, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description

WHAT IS THE OPPORTUNITY?

The Director, Finance Intelligent Automation & Controls within the Office of the US CFO will own the prototype-to-pilot pipeline for AI-enabled transformation across Regulatory Reporting, Financial Control, Product Control, and FP&A, personally building agentic AI prototypes that accelerate core finance production workflows while establishing governable, reusable technical patterns for enterprise productionization.

WHAT WILL YOU DO?

- Shape and execute the multi-year Finance AI roadmap across data, automation, AI, reporting, and workflow optimization – sequenced by addressable value and business impact rather than technology novelty
- Identify high-value AI use cases and personally build the first working agentic AI prototype against core production workflows (data sourcing, reconciliation, report production, variance commentary, review stack, inquiry response)
- Establish and track value-realization metrics including productivity gains, cycle-time reduction, reporting quality improvements, and decision support effectiveness
- Define the prototype-to-pilot hand-off pattern and technical standards that Technology teams will adopt to productionize solutions for enterprise scale
- Design for governance, audit, controls, and compliance from inception – establishing patterns for evaluation, human-in-the-loop approval, audit trails, and knowledge grounding across all solutions
- Partner with Technology and Data teams to identify and improve Finance data assets, quality, lineage, and accessibility to unblock AI delivery
- Build and sustain US Finance AI Academy – a structured upskilling program with communities of practice, adoption initiatives, and measurable outcomes across the Finance function
- Lead stakeholder management with senior Finance leadership, CFO organization, and global Technology/Data teams to influence design decisions and align priorities on investment
- Track emerging AI capability and maintain forward-looking adoption view, evaluating generative AI and agentic AI solutions without chasing tooling for its own sake
- Ensure every solution meets enterprise requirements for security, controls, compliance, audit, and resilience while applying agile delivery discipline
- Work in a fast-paced environment and prioritize work to meet deadlines.
- Provide thought leadership and work independently, while demonstrating strong attention to details.
- Perform additional responsibilities as requested to achieve business objectives.

WHAT DO YOU NEED TO SUCCEED?

Must have:
- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field; MBA or advanced technical credential preferred
- Minimum 12 years of progressive experience in Finance, with at least 5 years in senior leadership roles at a major financial institution
- Deep domain expertise across Regulatory Reporting, Financial Control, Product Control, or FP&A, demonstrating understanding of how financial numbers are produced, reviewed, and challenged
- Demonstrated hands-on AI/ML delivery experience: personally built and shipped LLM-based or agentic solutions in production environments (not sponsorship or oversight alone)
- Strong judgment in designing solutions for governance, audit, and controls from inception, with ability to discern genuinely solvable problems within current AI constraints
- Senior-level executive communication and credibility – capable of operating with direct CFO and ExCo visibility while influencing cross-functional decisions
- Proven builder's bias: comfortable producing working prototypes in days, iterating in front of stakeholders, and translating between domain and technical teams
- Technical fluency sufficient to direct (not necessarily build) modern AI/data stacks: Python, SQL, RAG and agentic frameworks, vector stores, cloud data platforms, and workflow orchestration
- Experience driving measurable adoption and change management at scale within complex, regulated environments

Nice-to-have :
- Capital markets product knowledge spanning rates, credit, equities, FX, and derivatives with familiarity to the trade lifecycle
- Foundational understanding of machine learning concepts sufficient to direct and evaluate model-based work
- Experience standing up upskilling programs, communities of practice, or capability centers within large Finance or Technology organizations
- Exposure to enterprise data governance, semantic layers, and metadata management frameworks

jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the Opportunity?
As the Senior Director, Strategy Risk Business Operations and Shared Services you will lead a high-performing team of directors, senior managers, and managers to drive strategic, operational, and financial excellence within RBC’s Commercial & Payment Technology (CPT) portfolio. This critical leadership role is accountable for Financial Management, Project Portfolio Planning, Vendor Management, Risk & Compliance, and Strategic Planning, ensuring alignment with enterprise priorities and delivering exceptional business outcomes. You will champion employee engagement, change management, and innovation (e.g., AI adoption) while maintaining rigorous governance and operational excellence.

Job Description

What is the opportunity?

RBC Capital Markets is seeking a high-performing Director or Vice President to join the Communications, Media, and Entertainment group within U.S. Corporate Banking, focused on Communications, Media, and Entertainment clients. This position entails full accountability for both relationship management and credit underwriting, serving as a senior coverage officer.

jobs.title: VP, Global Investment Banking, Mining & Metals
jobs.description:
Job Description

RBC Capital Markets is a part of the Royal Bank of Canada, one of the largest providers of financial services in the world with a purpose-driven, principles-led approach to delivering for our clients. RBC is a top ten bank globally and ranks among the top five banks in North America by market capitalization. In addition, RBC has one of the highest credit ratings of any financial institution globally.

Our Investment Banking division is a top 10 Global Investment Bank which is well-established in the largest, most mature capital markets across North America, Europe, and the Asia Pacific Regions.

Our Investment Banking division provides underwriting of equity and debt capital as well as strategic M&A advisory services for leading corporations, institutions, and governments throughout North America and around the world. We have built our successful investment banking business by focusing on our clients and the industry sectors in which they operate.
Our Mining & Metals group provides financial advice to a diverse range of public and private sector clients involved in building, owning and operating essential service infrastructure. With over 100 team members across North America, Europe, Australia and Asia, we offer clients insightful advice, bring a competitive advantage on funding solutions, and assist in navigating complex investment decisions.

What is the opportunity?

RBC Capital Markets is a part of the Royal Bank of Canada, one of the largest providers of financial services in the world. RBC ranks among the top five banks in North America by market capitalization and has one of the highest credit ratings of any financial institution globally.

Our Global Investment Banking division provides underwriting of equity and debt capital as well as strategic M&A advisory services for leading corporations, institutions and governments throughout North America and around the world. RBC Capital Markets is Canada’s leading investment bank. We have built our successful investment banking business by focusing on our clients and the industry sectors in which they operate. With teams located in North America, Europe, Australia and Asia, we offer clients across the public and private sectors insightful financial advice, bring a competitive advantage on funding solutions, and assist in navigating complex investment decisions.

What is the opportunity?

RBC Capital Markets Global Investment Banking division is seeking an Analyst to join the Diversified (“Consumer & Industrial Products”) team based in Toronto. The Consumer & Industrial Products team works across a variety of industries, including Consumer & Retail, Industrial, Communications, Media & Entertainment, Healthcare, Business Services and other. We support our clients through a variety of transactions including M&A, strategic alternative mandates, capital structure advisory and equity and debt financings. The Analyst role involves working collaboratively with product and coverage partners across RBC’s global platform to deliver the best advice possible to our clients.

The Analyst position is a unique opportunity to develop a broad financial skillset and gain exposure to global capital markets. The role is intended for individuals who wish to build a long-term career in Investment Banking with a market leading franchise and global platform.

- Supporting transaction structuring and execution efforts, with increasing levels of responsibility and accountability over time
- Financial and written analysis of companies and industries
- Contributing to the delivery of client meetings and presentations
- Conducting research to analyze market trends
- Researching and analyzing future opportunities
- Contribute to the execution of equity and debt financings, mergers and acquisitions, and financial advisory assignments

What do you need to succeed?

- - 1-2 years of investment banking, private equity, equity research, corporate development or advisory experience (corporate finance, transaction services, valuations, etc.)

jobs.description:
Job Description

What Will You Do?
The Senior Associate / Vice President will be responsible for the day-to-day execution of financing and advisory mandates and the management of deal workstreams, including:

Transaction Execution & Workstream Management
- Supporting and/or leading the day-to-day execution of project finance and advisory mandates, including managing timelines, deliverables, and workstream sequencing from mandate through closing
- Coordinating workflow across internal teams (coverage partners, product partners, syndications, corporate banking) and external service providers (legal counsel, rating agencies, independent engineers, insurance advisors, environmental consultants)
- Determining task sequencing and allocating assignments to analysts and junior associates on deal teams; establishing clear deliverable expectations and deadlines
- Reviewing and providing feedback on work product prepared by junior team members, including financial analysis, due diligence summaries, credit risk assessments, project summaries, rating report summaries, and market alternatives
- Overseeing the preparation and refinement of client presentations, information memoranda, and financing documentation
- Serving as a primary point of contact for clients on day-to-day transaction matters, managing expectations and communicating progress on workstreams
- Interfacing directly with counterparties including lenders, rating agencies, and advisors to advance transaction execution

Financial Analysis & Diligence
- Directing financial model analysis, debt sizing, and structuring work performed by junior resources; reviewing summary outputs and guiding refinements to assumptions and structure
- Reviewing independent engineer reports, market studies, and other third-party diligence materials to identify credit risks, key assumptions, and issues for escalation
- Synthesizing complex project and financial information into clear recommendations for senior bankers and clients

Business Development Support
- Supporting senior bankers in the pursuit of new business opportunities, including reviewing client-provided materials, evaluating transaction feasibility, and participating in client meetings and presentations
- Overseeing the development of pitch materials and responses to RFPs/RFIs

RBC Capital Markets is a part of the Royal Bank of Canada, one of the largest providers of financial services in the world with a purpose-driven, principles-led approach to delivering for our clients. You will be the orchestrating lead between executive sponsors, business leaders, and operational teams, coordinating complex initiatives that drive organizational transformation.

You will manage large transformational projects in Cash, Cheques and Payments and direct various stakeholder groups to deliver enterprise-wide transformation benefits while managing stakeholder priorities, program health, and strategic alignment across competing business objectives.  This pivotal role combines strategic vision with hands-on operational expertise, positioning you to drive organizational excellence through process optimization, artificial intelligence, automation and advanced reporting and data analytics.
Success is consistently delivering on transformational projects that achieve measurable improvements in process efficiency, operator productivity, operational risk reduction, as well as client and employee satisfaction.

jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the Opportunity?
An exciting opportunity to join Enterprise Controller (Wholesale Finance) team. The Associate Director, Commercial Banking Financial Control, will act as the subject matter expert and key point of contact for the Commercial Banking business in Canada, with the objective of delivering timely, accurate and reliable financial information. The people manager will support the internal and external reporting, disclosure requirements and control framework, as well as seek opportunities to streamline existing processes and lead ad-hoc projects, while liaising and collaborating with various stakeholders across the Enterprise.

What will you do?
- Ensure the accuracy and completeness of financial and regulatory reporting for supported business lines by reviewing monthly GL data, financial results and variances to ensure accuracy, including monitoring of allocations and other intergroup activities.
- Responsible to ensure new products and new transactions are appropriately captured in RBC financial reporting systems, and that appropriate accounting methodologies are applied. In particular, prepare analyses that take into account IFRS accounting implications and external and internal reporting requirements including MD&A, B/S, P&L, note disclosures & supplemental formats.
- Review the monthly Global Attestation review program to ensure proper financial controls supporting external financial results are in place.  Ensure that global policies and procedures are adhered to by all stakeholders including monitoring of allocations and other intergroup activities.
- Subject matter expert for deposits and lending products accounting issues. Maintain technical knowledge and ensure Financial Control, Product Control, and Business teams are kept abreast of all new accounting developments.
- Contribute and represent Finance function on various IT system projects/initiatives.
- Ensure SOX and RBC EUDA documentation compliance and completeness including new controls/processes.
- Participate in ad-hoc projects as directed by Director, Commercial Banking Financial Control.

What do you need to succeed?
Must-have
- CPA designation or equivalent. This mandate is highly dependent on using analytical and financial reporting skills commonly associated with accounting designations.
- Knowledge of relevant financial and regulatory accounting standards, especially IFRS 9.
- Strong communication, interpersonal and collaboration skills are considered necessary for the success of this role.

jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?

As an Alternatives Investment Strategist for RBC US Wealth Management you will work alongside the Multi-Asset Portfolio Strategist, Wealth Strategists, Alternatives Consultants and other internal teams on developing, coordinating, and executing our alternatives ambitions. The role is part of the Portfolio Advisory Group (PAG).  PAG’s mandate is to enable RBC-WM financial advisors to consistently deliver investment advice and solutions to their clients with the highest level of competence and confidence and your role will empower financial advisors with thoughts on the asset class and portfolio positioning.

What will you do?

- Responsible for internal and external publications about the alternatives market
- Organize and participate in webcasts focusing on alternatives topics and market outlook
- Collaborate with Marketing to support alternatives campaigns and enhance website content
- Collaborate with the U.S. Investment Committee and Global Portfolio Advisory Committee members to formulate market views across various alternative asset classes
- Assist UHNW advisors or other internal partners in review of client portfolios and allocations with specific focus on alternatives
- Create and implement a proactive service model for managing relationships
- Stay current on emerging trends in the alternatives market to make informed investment recommendations
- Create an actionable investment framework within the alternatives market to help advisors and clients understand risks and opportunities
- Communicate market (our cross-asset investment views) and economic perspectives to clients, via client presentations, publications or product-oriented marketing programs
- Relate key market developments to the positioning within managed portfolios to clients, specifically within alternative asset classes
- Research model portfolio development that includes alternative investments

What do you need to succeed?

Must-have

- Bachelor’s degree, preferably in Finance or Economics
- 10+ years’ financial industry experience
- 5+ years’ experience as an investment strategist or similar role
- Series 7 & 66 licensed or ability to obtain in 180 days
- Previous experience working with financial advisors
- Knowledge of complex investment structures and esoteric investments
- Exhibits wealth management and investment products expertise
- Able to listen to client’s needs and make decisions/take actions that help clients achieve their long-term goals
- Effective problem identification, analytical and resolution skills
- Ability to distill complex or detailed financial information into key points and a recommendation
- Knowledge of investment management disciplines such as asset allocation, portfolio construction, risk return analytics, performance measurement and reporting
- Strong ability to interact with all levels of staff. Must be able to maintain relationships that will relate to the overall success of the established firm goals

Nice-to-have

- CFA®, CAIA®, or CFP® designation or working to obtain
- 2+ years HNW client experience
- Portfolio management experience
- Experience in investment performance and risk analysis, particularly as it relates to multi-asset portfolio management
- Experience recommending and researching private investment opportunities and how they fit into a well-diversified high-net worth portfolio

What’s in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?
The Chief Investment Strategist (CIS) for RBC Phillips, Hager & North Investment Counsel Inc. (“PH&N IC”) will be responsible for the curation, development and monitoring of the firm’s investment platform that spans all asset classes, geographies and investment vehicles. Further, the CIS provides leadership on the PH&N IC’s firm-led investment philosophy, portfolio construction and risks management frameworks through regular communication with the Investment Counsellors and their clients.

Reporting to the President of PH&N IC, the individual will lead the development, execution, training and communication of PH&N IC’s strategic asset allocation models, and related tactical asset allocation recommendations to Investment Counsellors. The Chief Investment Strategist will act as a spokesperson for the business, and possibly at times on behalf of RBC Wealth Management Canada (WMC). For more information, please visit:  RBC PH&N Investment Counsel Inc.

What will you do?
- Provide leadership to develop strategic direction of the firm’s curated investment platform across all asset classes, geographies and investment vehicles.
- Chair the RBC PH&N Investment Committee that collectively stewards the platform via regular monitoring and product due diligence while concurrently ensuring accountability of product managers on the shelf.
- Work with key partners such as RBC Global Asset Management, Global Manager Research, and the WMC Alternatives team on the review of proprietary and sub-advised solutions.
- Develop and communicate PH&N IC’s firm led investment philosophy with respect to asset allocation, portfolio construction and risk management to drive greater consistency and risk mitigation across client portfolios.
- Formulate investment strategy opinions and recommendations for PH&N IC in conjunction with internal partners.
- Act as an ambassador for PH&N IC by cultivating strong partnerships and relationships across RBC to drive a greater understanding of our firm’s differentiated investment process, and competitive value proposition.
- Work with partners (e.g. Private Banking, Enterprise Strategic Client Group or RBC Capital Markets) to drive more holistic and comprehensive investment solutions to augment our overall offering and ultimately drive better client experiences
- Represent PH&N IC in public events and speaking engagements. The CIS will act as a spokesperson for the business, and possibly at times on behalf of RBC Wealth Management Canada on mainstream and social media outlets.
- Lead the content creation and communication of timely investment-related publications and video-recordings to Investment Counsellors and clients.
- Acts as business subject matter expert / representative on key strategic cross-enterprise initiatives / committees related to investments.
- Maintain active profile with Investment Counsellors via consistent office presence, written communication and presentations.
- Training and Development of Investment Counsellors through ongoing portfolio construction training sessions throughout the year (target 3-4x per year).
- Explore portfolio management / risk management technologies that could enhance Investment Counsellor efficiency and AUM consolidation to support PH&N IC growth targets.
- Lead by demonstrating commitment to ownership of client concerns related to portfolio / trading errors and complaints at first point of contact ensuring the escalation process for Client Problem Resolution is followed creating a differentiated client experience.
- Be highly visible as a leader across the broader PH&N IC National Office team, ensuring a high level of engagement and awareness of team strategy, priorities and successes, fostering a high performing One RBC client-centric culture. Build effective teams by actively recruiting and supporting their development through strong relationship management practices, coaching sessions, staff reviews, and performance management.

What do you need to succeed?

- 10+ years in a senior investment management role preferably in the PH&N IC related industry segment
- 5+ years of strong strategic and project management experience
- Extensive knowledge of public and private markets, custody solutions, investment solutions with the ability to remain current on related issues

- Prior experience directly with RBC / PH&N IC

jobs.title: Analyst, Global Investment Banking - Real Estate
jobs.description:
Job Description
RBC Capital Markets is a part of the Royal Bank of Canada, one of the largest providers of financial services in the world. RBC ranks among the top five banks in North America by market capitalization and has one of the highest credit ratings of any financial institution globally.

Our Global Investment Banking division provides underwriting of equity and debt capital as well as strategic M&A advisory services for leading corporations, institutions and governments throughout North America and around the world. RBC Capital Markets is Canada’s leading investment bank. We have built our successful investment banking business by focusing on our clients and the industry sectors in which they operate.

With teams located in North America, Europe, Australia and Asia, we offer clients across the public and private sectors insightful financial advice, bring a competitive advantage on funding solutions, and assist in navigating complex investment decisions.

What is the opportunity?

RBC Capital Markets Global Investment Banking is seeking an Analyst to join its Real Estate investment banking team in Toronto.

RBC Capital Markets Real Estate Group is the largest dedicated real estate corporate finance group in Canada, with offices in Toronto, Montréal, Calgary, and New York. The Group’s capabilities span Equity and Debt Capital Markets, Mergers & Acquisitions, and Advisory & Valuation for public, private, corporate and government owners of real estate. Our highly experienced team works closely with the firm’s M&A, ECM, DCM, and Leveraged Finance professionals to advise clients.

What will you do?
- Evaluate and analyze the financial needs of clients, including developing complex financial models

- Support transaction structuring and execution efforts, with increasing levels of responsibility and accountability over time

- Financial and written analysis of companies and industries

- Contributing to the delivery of client meetings and presentations

- Conducting research to analyze market trends

- Researching and analyzing future opportunities

- Contribute to the execution of equity and debt financings, mergers and acquisitions, and financial advisory assignments

What do you need to succeed?
- Undergraduate degree program in Finance, Accounting, Engineering or a quantitative field from a leading university

- Strong quantitative skills focused on financial analysis, accounting and financial theory

- Strong verbal and written communication skills

- A high level of attention to detail

- Ability to manage multiple competing priorities and thrive in a fast-paced and challenging environment

- Value and possess strong competency in the following behaviours: Collaboration, Relationship Building, Communication, Integrity and Operating with Diverse and Inclusive Mindset

- The ability to perform effectively in a team environment and excel under pressure amid demanding deadlines

- Well-rounded set of interests and extra-curricular activities beyond academics

- Desire to develop a leadership skillset and make meaningful contributions in a fast-paced, team environment

- CFA, CPA or other relevant professional designations are considered an asset, but not a requirement

- 1-2 years of investment banking, private equity, equity research, M&A / corporate development or accounting experience an asset, but not required

What’s in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, think progressively, continue our growth, and deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our individual / collective potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

From this experience you will gain:
- A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation

- A strong foundation in fundamental investment banking skills such as financial modeling and analysis, transaction execution and negotiation, and in-depth industry and product knowledge

- Experience working in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team

- Leaders who support your development through coaching and mentoring opportunities

- Ability to make a difference through impactful transactions which help shape an industry

- Develop an analytical skillset through real world transaction experience

- Gain exposure and insight into the global capital markets

- Work directly with senior levels of Canada’s largest and fastest growing companies

- Build a long-term career in Investment Banking

- Opportunities to do challenging work

- Flexible work/life balance options

Required Documents: Cover letter, Resume and Academic Transcripts (unofficial are acceptable) in one PDF document. Please ensure you submit these three documents in one PDF document under the “resume” section. Do not submit them separately.

Each year, we invite rising second-year MBA students to join our Global Investment Banking (GIB) platform for a 10-week U.S. Summer Associate Program. The program provides an opportunity for you to experience the culture and atmosphere of RBC Capital Markets and experience the role of a full-time Associate.

What will you do?

GIB provides a complete suite of strategic advisory services, as well as equity and debt capital raising capabilities for leading corporations, institutions and governments. RBC Capital Markets’ investment banking platform focuses on nine core industries and seven product groups. Our San Francisco office recruits for the following industry and product groups:

Industry Group:
- Technology

Product Group:
- Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A)

Similar to full-time GIB Associates, summer associates will spend their time:
- Working on a variety of live transactions and client-facing business development initiatives in all areas of GIB
- Developing and preserving complex financial models
- Contributing to the delivery of client meetings and presentations
- Conducting research to analyze market trends
- Researching and analyzing future opportunities

What do you need to succeed?

In selecting summer associates, we look for the following:
- Students in their penultimate year of study at an accredited 2-year MBA program
- 2+ years’ work post-undergraduate work experience
- Ability to manage multiple competing priorities and thrive in a fast-paced and challenging environment
- Value and possess strong competency in the following behaviors: Collaboration, Relationship Building, Communication, Integrity and Operating with Diverse and Inclusive Mindset
- Well-rounded set of interests and extra-curricular activities beyond academics

What’s in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, think progressively, continue our growth, and deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our individual/collective potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

From this experience you would gain:
- A strong foundation in fundamental investment banking skills such as financial modeling and analysis, transaction execution and negotiation, and in-depth industry/product knowledge
- A better understanding of RBC’s products and services
- The support of a mentor (typically a full-time Associate or Vice President)
- An opportunity to network and discuss career opportunities through a number of social events

The good faith expected salary range for the above position is $175,000 depending on factors including but not limited to: the candidate’s experience, skills, registration status, market conditions, and business needs. RBC’s compensation philosophy and principles recognize the importance of a highly qualified global workforce and plays a critical role in attracting, engaging and retaining talent that:

Job Description

- Vice President, Senior Front Office Quant, RBC Capital Markets, LLC, New York, NY:

Responsible to apply quantitative and programming skills to research, develop, test, and implement securitized products and structured credit pricing / default / loss models. Build and maintain agency and non-agency mortgage prepayment and default models. Build front office analytic tools for trading and risk. Effectively collaborate with traders, risk managers, IT and other functions to support trading activities. Identify operational risk/ control deficiencies in the business. Review and comply with Firm Policies applicable to Central Funding Group (CFG) business activities (funding, trading, and investment). Escalate operational risk loss events, control deficiencies and risks that are identified to line manager and the relevant control functions on a timely basis. Conduct data analysis, simulation and forecasting with statistical and machine learning techniques. Leverage object-oriented programming (OOP) principles, utilizing C++, Python and R programming languages to implement high performance model libraries. Integrate prepayment models into PolyPaths system with Intex. Construct and maintain databases for ensuring persistence and availability of mortgage-backed securities data (EMBS, Intex and CoreLogic).

Telecommuting permitted up to 1 day per week.

#LI-DNI

Full time employment, Monday – Friday, 40 hours per week, $210,000.00 per year.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

Master’s degree in Financial Engineering, Quantitative Finance, Computational Finance & Risk Management or a related field and 4 years of related work experience.

Must have 3 years of experience in:

* Using Python to develop and deploy quantitative models, build and maintain data pipelines, process large-scale datasets, integrate with cloud computing environments.
* Automate analytics and reporting workflows for trading or financial applications.
* Using C++ to develop and maintain pricing and valuation libraries for fixed income or structured products, support legacy quantitative systems, implement unit testing, optimize performance.

Job Description

The Senior Manager Operations (CCAO) is a key leadership role responsible for supporting the VP Client Complaints Appeals Office. As the incumbent, you will play a critical role in ensuring operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement across all facets of the CCAO function. You will work collaboratively across the organization to drive objective complaint resolution while supporting the operational and compliance soundness of the business unit.

Operations Leadership (50%)
- Support team leadership in enabling successful completion of investigations in adherence with the Financial Consumer Protection Framework (FCPF) and Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC) guidelines
- Drive ongoing review and enhancement of the team operating model to effectively address escalations from the External Complaints Body (Level 4 within the progressive escalation model)
- Support enhancement of data capture, monitoring, and reporting capabilities, reducing manual processes and developing insights-driven reporting
- Collaborate with CART and Case IQ platforms to strengthen reporting and decision-making across all operational facets

Stakeholder Collaboration & Communication (20%)
- Work with internal stakeholders to identify process, policy, and approach gaps; share coaching opportunities and drive continuous improvement
- Support external and internal communication strategies, including presentations to senior management and external regulatory bodies
- Maintain weekly reconciliation of Case IQ L4 closed cases versus OBSI Portal; track and report on OBSI Pilot Project results
- Deliver bi-weekly closed case results and quarterly L3/L4 results reporting

Risk Management & Compliance (Embedded across all responsibilities)
- Execute Risk and Control Self-Assessments (RCSA) to identify operational risks and validate effectiveness of control activities
- Conduct annual Supplier Risk Management Assessments (SRMA) for critical third-party vendors supporting CCAO operations
- Develop and maintain Business Continuity Plans ensuring critical processes remain operational during disruptions
- Oversee IT application management, including system health assessments and access controls (CART, Case IQ platforms)
- Establish and monitor Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) aligned with organizational risk tolerance
- Conduct semi-annual system access reviews to ensure appropriate segregation of duties and compliance with SOX requirements
- Support execution of SOC 2 attestation requirements

Reporting & External Accountability (15%)
- Accountable for supporting the development and publication of the CCAO annual report to the public within prescribed timelines, accessible on RBC's website
- Support the VP CCAO in executing an effective communication plan with weekly, bi-weekly, and quarterly reporting deliverables: - Weekly comparison of Case IQ L4 Closed Cases vs. OBSI Portal discrepancies
- Weekly OBSI Pilot Project results tracking
- Bi-weekly closed case results
- Quarterly L3 and L4 results reporting

Personal Learning & Development (15%)
- Conduct research on internal dispute resolution frameworks and methodologies; benchmark with industry peers to enhance CCAO processes
- Stay current with regulatory requirements (FCAC, OSFI, CBA standards) and emerging best practices in complaint resolution
- Support team capability elevation through continued coaching and professional development initiative

- Experience: - 10–20 years of experience in diverse roles across the three lines of defence (client-facing, risk, compliance, audit functions)
- Demonstrated experience leading and managing through organizational change
- Proven experience conducting operational risk reviews of vendor-provided applications and controls
- Project management experience with ability to deliver multiple competing priorities
- Experience in complaint resolution, dispute management, or regulatory compliance environments

- Technical Skills: - Advanced proficiency with data analysis, reporting tools, and business intelligence platforms
- Strong knowledge of financial services regulation (FCPF, FCAC guidelines, OSFI standards)
- Familiarity with case management systems, risk assessment frameworks, and internal control methodologies
- Bilingual proficiency (French and English) in written and spoken communication is a nice to have
- Prior experience with regulatory bodies (FCAC, OSFI, CIRO, OBSI) or external complaint resolution mechanisms
- Familiarity with SOX compliance frameworks and control testing methodologies
- Experience with business continuity planning and disaster recovery

Access Management, Adaptability, Building Dashboards, Business Reporting, Communication, Customer Relationship Management (CRM), Decision Making, Detail-Oriented, Ethical Business, Group Problem Solving, Negotiation, Organizational Savvy and Politics, Report Writing, Results-Oriented, Risk Assessments, Stakeholder Engagement

Role includes managing the implementation, configuration, and development of incentive management systems used to manage monthly, quarterly, and annual incentive payments across multiple business lines. The player-coach will ensure accuracy of payout calculations, compliance with governance and business objectives, and reporting and analyses, while maintaining the system for new and changing business requirements.

As an RBC Ambassador, you create value at the moments that matter most to newcomers and help them achieve their goals by collaborating with your colleagues and partners at RBC. The successful candidate will be responsible for developing partnerships with local community organizations that support newcomers' settlement. This role, which requires mobility and flexibility, is key to organizing and delivering advisory events for community partners. This unique position leverages your expertise in digital advising and your ability to build internal and external Together at RBC partnerships to maximize interactions.
Specifically, you and your team will address the everyday banking, credit, and investment needs of both clients and non-clients (primarily newcomers), as well as other needs that extend beyond traditional banking services. Whether you're showing newcomers how to use digital banking, assisting with their onboarding as new clients, referring them to a specialist for their more complex transactions, or providing guidance beyond RBC's standard offerings—for example, on adapting to Canadian culture, understanding community needs, or entering the job market—your expertise will contribute to delivering a memorable experience that fosters satisfaction and loyalty.

You will work from home and will be required to travel within the market.

- Focus on educating newcomers, including through demonstrations, and leverage technology to deliver a memorable customer experience, enhance the brand, and build customer loyalty.

jobs.title: Senior Marketing Manager, Home Equity Finance
jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?
RBC Home Equity Financing is one of Canada’s most significant and strategically vital lending businesses — and we’re looking for a Senior Marketing Manager to be part of the next chapter of growth for this exciting portfolio.
The Canadian mortgage space is a dynamic space that continues to evolve. A single decision represents the largest financial commitment most Canadians will ever make, so emotion, trust, and life's biggest milestones meet hard numbers and real competition. It calls for marketers who can balance brand storytelling with performance rigor, who can move potential home buyers from a dream to a decision.
As the Senior Marketing Manager, Home Equity Financing, you will shape and drive integrated marketing strategies across mass advertising, digital and programmatic.
If you are a bold, results-oriented marketer who thrives on turning complex challenges into breakthrough campaigns — and you have a track record of delivering integrated, multi-channel programs at scale that move the needle on acquisition — this is your opportunity to shape how millions of Canadians experience one of the most pivotal moments of their financial lives.

What will you do?
Integrated Campaign Planning and Execution
- Build a strong working relationship with an extensive network of internal partners and leverage your ability to impact and influence partnerships across the Bank.
- Own and lead best-in-class mass integrated campaign planning and go-to-market execution across owned and paid channels.
- Develop and deliver creative and media briefs, tactical plans and collaborate with agency partners and external vendors to deliver high-quality creative and media executions on time and on budget.
- Proactively seek out new growth opportunities, campaign innovation and test initiatives to drive continuous improvement and learning.
- Partner closely with the performance marketing team to drive year-round acquisition initiatives, ensuring we are efficiently scaling acquisition growth and maximizing ROI, and translating data into clear, actionable recommendations.
- Lead targeted acquisition campaigns that activate field sales and owned digital channels, building a seamless journey from first impression to funded mortgage.
- Keep a keen eye to process to drive efficiencies and excellence across all stages.
- Manage marketing budget efficiently, focusing on transparency, efficiency, and flexibility to make the most of market opportunities.

Measurement & Performance Reporting
- Monitor, report and present marketing results to line-of-business stakeholders providing data-driven recommendations to optimize campaigns to drive growth.
- Translate marketing performance metrics into clear business outcomes, articulating the “so what” for the line of business and recommending where to double down or course-correct.
- Lead the cross-functional development of Spring campaign lead reporting collaborating with Digital Marketing Partners
- Oversee the development and communication of monthly lead results.

Team Leadership & People Development
- Lead, mentor, and develop two marketing managers, setting clear direction, maintaining high standards, and creating conditions for sustained excellence
- Provide strong people management, including coaching, performance development, career planning, and recognition
- Model inclusive leadership behaviours consistent with RBC’s values and Purpose

What do you need to succeed?
Must-have:
- 7+ years marketing experience, with demonstrated ability to think strategically.
- Experience planning, managing, and optimizing multi-million dollar marketing budget with rigorous measurement and accountability
- Strong analytical capabilities; comfort with data, performance metrics, and a fact-based approach to decision-making and executive communication
- Proven project management and organizational skills. Ability to multi-task, as well as confidently and effectively lead a project team through timelines, prioritization, budget management and collaboration.
- Ability to influence peers and partners through collaborative, transparent socialization, to secure alignment on our vision and recommendations.
- Ability to think strategically and execute with excellence; must be an enthusiastic, well-organized self-starter, able to use initiative and adapt to change within a fast-paced environment.
- Strong attention to detail and ability to lead multi-stakeholder groups to develop and execute targeted marketing campaigns.
- A growth mindset and a strong track record of insight-led marketing in a culture that values a collaborative approach.
- 3+ years of people management experience, with a demonstrated track record of building and leading high-performing teams

Nice-to-have:
- FI experience an asset and/or experience in large matrix organizations.
- University degree - undergraduate and/or MBA - in marketing or other related field
- Mass marketing experience.
- Direct experience marketing mortgage, HELOC, or secured lending products
- Experience in a large financial institution or similarly regulated, complex matrix environment

What’s in it for you?
We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.
- A high-impact, highly visible role at the heart of one of RBC’s most strategically important consumer lending businesses
- The opportunity to lead an exceptional team and own end-to-end marketing accountability across a major portfolio
- A competitive total compensation package including base salary, performance-based incentive, and comprehensive benefits
- Opportunities to take on progressively greater accountabilities and grow your career at Canada’s largest bank

What is the opportunity?

We are looking for a commercially minded, entrepreneurial leader with deep experience in the data product and alternative data ecosystem to help build differentiated data products and expand our connectivity across the external innovation landscape.

Sitting at the intersection of data, product, clients and innovation, this role will shape and commercialize strategic data products in close partnership with our Alternative Data Insights and Sales teams. The role will also serve as a key external connector for Innovation Foundry, working across Technology Banking, fintechs and technology companies to identify and advance new opportunities across Capital Markets and RBC.

We are looking for someone who can understand the client, spot the opportunity, shape the product, build the partnership and connect the right people to bring it to market.

What you'll do
Data Products & Commercialization
- Partner closely with Sales as the data product expert, positioning and growing differentiated products with hedge funds, asset managers and other institutional clients.

- Build deep client relationships to understand investment workflows, unmet needs and emerging alternative data use cases.

- Shape the product vision and commercial proposition, translating unique datasets and client needs into differentiated products.

- Lead product positioning, client pitches and go-to-market strategy in partnership with Sales and Alternative Data Insights.

What is the Opportunity?
The Workday Solutions Senior Manager is the functional backbone and people leader for RBC's Workday platform, accountable for its Design integrity—configuration, integrations, data model, and security. This role ensures the platform remains stable, governable, and extensible.

The Senior Manager Workday Solutions Designer, governs, and evolves RBC's Workday technical design within HRDS, while leading a team of functional configuration, security and data analysts. The role combines hands-on experience (configuration design, security and data) with solutions design and people leadership across the Workday Platform — ensuring consistency, scalability, and compliance as the platform grows, and that the team executing the work is well-managed and developing.

People Leadership

Job Description

RBC Real Estate Capital Partners

RBC Real Estate Capital Partners (RECP) is a leading provider of debt capital to premier, institutional real estate sponsors. RECP’s mandate is to originate debt secured by stabilized and transitional assets across all major commercial real estate asset classes, in both single asset and portfolio investments. RECP acts as principal, deploying RBC Capital Markets’ balance sheet by originating senior mortgage, mezzanine, loan-on-loan, and revolving facilities.

RECP focuses on core and major regional markets in the US, UK, Europe, Australia, and Canada. With a small team of dedicated professionals in Dallas and London, over the past decade RECP has participated in over $42 billion of mortgage, mezzanine and loan-on-loan financings.

What is the opportunity?

RECP Dallas is looking for a qualified real estate professional to oversee RECP’s North American and Australian loan book, with a focus on the supervision of RECP’s exposure and the active management of loan positions. Together with the originations team, the candidate will maintain relationships with client contacts in the US, Australia, and Canada, as well as internal RBC partners in critical support groups based in Toronto and NY.

What will you do?

- Develop and lead strategic initiatives to enhance and optimize the asset management platform
- Active monitoring of the RECP Dallas loan portfolio, which is comprised of assets in the US, Australia, and Canada, while regularly engaging with internal and external stakeholders
- Provide direction and assistance to asset management Analysts / Associates
- Analyze and approve key deal-level decisions, including lease approvals, and coordinate potential facility modifications
- Contribute to and oversee the ongoing production of comprehensive portfolio review and analysis presentations (e.g. revenue forecasts, stress tests, exposure concentration analyses, etc.)
- Lead recurring Asset Management Updates, which include ongoing qualitative and quantitative analysis of the RECP loan portfolio and real estate collateral
- Oversee third party loan servicers and internal RBC transaction management teams in monitoring of loan covenants and performance
- Interact with borrowers to get regular, detailed performance updates on the real estate assets collateralizing the portfolio
- Participate in site inspections of ongoing capital work and evaluate business plan execution progress
- Prepare co-lender reporting packages, where applicable, while managing information requests and consents required by co-lenders on lender approval requests received from borrowers
- Manage external and internal reviews of the loan portfolio

What do you need to succeed?

- Bachelor’s degree or higher
- 10+ years of experience in the commercial real estate sector (asset management, servicing, banking, finance or investing)
- Robust verbal and written presentation capabilities
- Excellent data management and Excel cash flow modelling skills
- Argus experience
- Self-motivated, with ability to work both autonomously and in a highly collaborative, team based environment
- Ability to prioritize, multi-task and meet tight timelines
- Willingness and ability to travel

jobs.title: Senior Risk Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the Opportunity?
As the Senior Risk Analyst, you will safeguard City National Bank's digital assets and technological infrastructure by implementing risk management procedures that secure IT infrastructure and data while meeting compliance and regulatory standards. You will identify and mitigate IT, regulatory, and operational risks, and support the maintenance of operational and IT control procedures.

You will collaborate with a variety of stakeholders and will translate IT risks into actionable insights. You will review key risk indicators (KRI) reports, gather and validate risk metrics, and equip stakeholders with accurate information to drive informed decision making.

This dynamic position provides opportunities for working across the organization and playing a key role in risk mitigation.

What will you do?
- Identify, evaluate, and address risks to ensure regulatory and compliance alignment while supporting the overall risk management framework
- Act as first line of defense, filtering and routing issues to the correct stakeholders
- Own IT risk findings end-to-end, ensuring all dependent tasks are completed and escalated appropriately
- Analytics & Metrics: Validate data accuracy in risk dashboards, prepare monthly reports on issue status and KRIs, and identify critical actions
- Determine appropriate escalation paths and communicate with IT application owners, portfolio managers, and leadership
- Evaluate risks against industry frameworks (PCI, NIST, IS027001, ITGC) document findings in Archer and track remediation in ServiceNow
- Work across IT application owners, portfolio managers, and audit teams without direct authority; communicate risk profiles and business impact clearly
- Control Deficiency Management: Coordinate with stakeholders to log, manage, and track control deficiencies. Assess remediation plans to ensure they are designed to effectively reduce risk and verify that corrective actions are implemented according to plan
- Perform risk-based control assessments to evaluate the design, implementation, and operating effectiveness of IT and Operational Controls.
- Compliance Support: Understand audit functions, evidence workflows, and compensating control processes to support regulatory requirements

What do you need to succeed?

Must have:
- 3+ years of experience in Information/Cyber Security, IT Risk Management, IT Operations, or Technology, with at least 2+ years focused on controls testing, internal audit, quality control, risk management, or compliance
- Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business or a related field
- Solid knowledge of IT General Computing Controls and Application Controls
- Experience with Application Control Assessments and Infrastructure Control Assessments
- Experience in design, execution and reporting of Key risk indicators (KRI)
- Experience in first line of defense
- Previous experience explaining controls, risks and gaps to both technical and non-technical audiences, including engaging with vendors and internal teams
- Knowledge of cyber security technologies such as access control solutions, authentication, network security, cryptography, PCI, privacy and data classification/protection
- Excellent written and oral communication skills
- Understanding of third line functions and audit processes (evidence request workflows, compensating controls)
- General awareness of infrastructure risks (IAM, firewalls, network security, database security—SQL/Oracle, cloud)

Nice to have:
- Big Four (4) IT risk consulting and/or audit experience
- Accredited certification / designation such as CISA / CISSP / CIA / CRISC or similar
- Knowledge of OSFI, FINRA, SEC, MSRB, FRBNY and OCC rules and regulations
- Strong knowledge of rules, regulations and compliance requirements for the financial services industry concerning hybrid cloud and multiple technology domains
- Experience with Archer findings documentation, and ServiceNow issue tracking

What’s in it for you?
We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

- Ability to make a difference and lasting impact.

- Opportunities to do challenging work
- Opportunities to take on progressively greater accountabilities

What is the Opportunity?
We are looking for a visionary and results driven Director of Conversational Banking with a passion for building intelligent conversational AI systems for customer experience across web and mobile platforms. You will be developing and creating innovative technology solutions powering growth and improving client experience leading a team of talented full stack developers and conversational AI engineers. WHAT WILL YOU DO?
- Develop and execute the technology roadmap for conversational banking practice within Advice Center, Branch Technology and Martech, driving significant growth in revenue, market share, and client adoption across various industries.
- Lead the delivery and development team of Conversational Architects, designers, and developers in building complex, high-quality conversational AI solution.
- Identify new business opportunities and cultivate strong relationships with key partners, stakeholders, and within client organizations to expand our footprint.
- Lead the entire lifecycle of solution development and delivery, from conceptualization and design to implementation, optimization, and ongoing support, focusing on platform-agnostic best practices.
- Establish and manage key performance indicators (KPIs) for the practice and the delivered solutions, regularly reporting on progress and demonstrating tangible business value.
- Stay updated of the latest advancements in conversational AI platforms, generative AI and broader customer engagement technologies, integrating new capabilities into our offerings.
- Foster a culture of continuous learning and innovation within the team, encouraging experimentation and the adoption of cutting-edge techniques.
- Provide strong technical and strategic leadership, fostering a collaborative, high-performance, and client-centric team environment.
- Develop and implement training programs to ensure the team possesses the necessary skills in conversational AI design, architecture, and development.
- Manage resource allocation, project prioritization, and operational efficiency within the practice.
- Act as a trusted advisor to business partners, understanding their business challenges and translating them into effective Conversational AI solutions.

WHAT DO YOU NEED TO SUCCEED?

Must Haves:
- 10+ years of progressive experience in technology implementation, digital transformation, or customer experience roles, with a strong focus on AI/ML solutions.
- 5+ years of leadership experience leading and mentoring a development and delivery team of Conversational AI developers.
- Proven expertise and hands-on experience in leading the design, development, and delivery of large-scale, enterprise-level conversational AI solutions (e.g., chatbots, voicebots, virtual assistants).
- Deep knowledge of conversational AI best practices, including natural language processing (NLP), intent recognition, entity extraction, conversational flow design, LLMs, MCP, AI agents etc
- Demonstrated track record of successfully delivering large-scale AI/ML projects for enterprise clients, particularly in the customer service domain.
- Ability to pivot under business pressures in a rapidly changing landscape
- Hands on experience delivering/deploying/hardening applications and/or platforms
- Thorough understanding of operations and SRE principles at scale
- Strong understanding of contact center operations, customer journey mapping, and key customer experience metrics.
- Excellent business acumen with the ability to identify client needs, develop compelling value propositions to drive revenue growth.
- Exceptional communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage effectively with executive-level stakeholders and technical teams.
- Proven ability to influence and collaborate across diverse internal and external stakeholders.
- Strategic thinker with a strong problem-solving orientation and the ability to navigate complex business challenges.

Nice to have:
- Experience of implementing NLU/LLM solutions for multi-modal platforms.

jobs.description:

What is the opportunity?
This unique position calls on your client-focused sales expertise and natural problem-solving skills to maximize each client interaction. Specifically, you help clients with their everyday banking, credit, and investment needs. As an RBC ambassador, you add value in the moments that matter most to clients and collaborate with RBC partners to help clients achieve their goals. Whether you’re demonstrating to a client how to use digital banking, on-boarding a new client, or referring a complex opportunity to a specialist, your expertise will contribute to creating meaningful and memorable client experiences to drive client satisfaction and loyalty.

- Proactively engage with clients in all areas of the branch and in the community, uncovering banking needs, providing help and advice, as well as identifying sales and referral opportunities
- Focus on client education and demonstration, leveraging technology to deliver a memorable client experience, drive sales, and retain business
- Respond to client-initiated contact, assisting them with a full range of financial transactions
- Actively listen and engage clients in conversation to further understand their individual needs
- Proactively take ownership of resolving and preventing client banking problems
- Cultivate and maintain relationships with partners to make the most of business opportunities and referrals

Must-have
- Mutual Funds accreditation, or willingness to obtain it (i.e., Investment Funds in Canada or the Canadian Securities Course)
- Demonstrated passion for putting clients first, as well as success in a hands-on, target-driven sales environment
- Problem-solving and people skills, with the ability to build strong relationships and proactively connect with clients
- Flexibility, eagerness to learn, strong personal ethics, and a hunger for success
- Digital literacy across a broad range of devices (i.e., smartphones, tablets, laptops, etc.)
- Availability to work all open business hours
