jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the Opportunity?

As part of the Group Risk Management (GRM) team, the Director, Corporate Insurance Risk Management (CIRM) will oversee the annual insurance renewal program to enable CIRM to fulfill its mandate and achieve its objectives. This role partners and collaborates closely with other CIRM Team members, internal stakeholders and external partners to oversee the renewal process; advise stakeholders across RBC on M&A and other insurance advisory requests; support claims management activities and processes; and continuously identifies opportunities to optimize RBC’s insurance program.
The Director, Corporate Insurance Risk Management will report to the Vice President, Third Party, Business Continuity, Crisis and Corporate Insurance Risk Management.

Note: This is a Maternity Leave coverage for 12 Months with option to extend depending on business needs

What will you do?
- Uphold the strategy, culture and activities that enable the team to operate as an integrated department
- Support a culture of integrity and behaviors that align to RBC’s Code of Conduct and professional standards
- Work collaboratively with the CIRM Team and across teams, contributing to an engaged workforce who are effective, knowledgeable and adaptable
- Foster an environment of continuous personal growth
- Act as the key point of contact in managing productive relationships with industry partners, including insurance brokers, insurers, legal counsel, peers, and consultants as required
- Oversee the annual insurance renewal/purchase process, including property and casualty, with financial lines experience an asset
- Review of insurance binders, policies, endorsements upon renewal to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with terms bound
- Review of the global program premium methodology and determine premium allocation
- Continuously identify opportunities to optimize and evolve RBC’s insurance program within the risk appetite
- Identify new and emerging risks and manage with potential insurance solutions
- Preparation of informational insurance summaries as required
- Contribute to initiatives as requested
- Advise RBC partners on insurance aspects of mergers & acquisitions, divestitures, new products and services to manage and mitigate risks
- Respond to regulatory inquiries and due diligence requests for information about RBC’s insurance
- Oversee the process of providing guidance and recommendations with the review of insurance provisions in vendor/supplier agreements, leases, and other documents as required
- Support the Claims Manager by providing advice and expertise regarding the management of claims where required
- Contribute to the annual Corporate Insurance Review for RBC Board of Directors reporting and local subsidiary board reporting
- Conduct research and analysis to identify new and emerging risks and trends to recommend loss transfer solutions
- Provide RBC business units with insurance training to support the review of supplier vendor contracts
- Other CIRM training/awareness as needed

What do you need to succeed?

Must Have
- Minimum of 10 yrs experience in either risk management, claims, underwriting, brokerage experience or similar experience (e.g. paralegal)
- Proficient in insurance contract reviews and understanding insurance policies
- Experience in risk management (1LOD or 2LOD) or related field, knowledge of financial services products, processes, and regulatory environment
- Experience working in a matrixed environment, and coordination of work across a large number of stakeholders
- Ability to foster collaborative relationships with partners across 1st and 2nd LOD and with key external partners

Nice to Have
- Familiar with the lifecycle of insurance purchase and renewal
- Knowledge of alternative risk transfer products and programs
- Proficiency with Bank technology- Knowledge  of Microsoft Applications - at a minimum Basic Word, Excel, Power Point.
- Advanced oral and written communication skills, including presentation and training skills
- Strong ability to influence through personal style and finesse rather than authority
- Advanced research skills – attuned to industry trends, events
- Analytical mind – ability to break down and work through complex problems in a detailed, accurate, and complete manner
- Proven ability to anticipate and identify risks and effective mitigants
- Action oriented, proactive with a high degree of initiative
- Ability to prioritize and work in a deadline driven environment
- Drives change and encourages continuous improvement of procedures and processes

What’s in it for you?
We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

Do you thrive in working in an interactive team environment? Do you have an interest in corporate real estate? Do you have strong written and spoken communication skills?

As an Analyst/Associate in our Real Estate Credit Transaction Management team, you will work closely with our Real Estate Corporate Banking teams in Toronto and New York to support the growth of our real estate lending portfolio, and you will manage a portfolio of real estate clients within the Global Corporate Banking division of RBC Capital Markets. You will also work closely with other groups within Capital Markets and the Bank to deliver a full range of credit and banking services to corporate clients of the Bank.

Please note: This role can be at the Analyst or Associate level, depending on the incumbent's background and skillset.

What will you do?
You will have an assigned portfolio of real estate clients and borrowers, and you will be responsible for the administration of your team's portfolio, which includes major real estate developers, REITs, and other significant real estate lending relationships. Your key responsibilities will include:

- Credit Underwriting & Analysis: Provide underwriting analysis of real estate credit transactions, including origination of new credit facilities, refinancings, renewals, and covenant amendments/waivers, with comprehensive financial and asset-level evaluation of corporate clients. Your responsibilities include: (i) Prepare detailed credit submissions and underwriting memos for submission to commitments committees; (ii) Conduct in-depth financial analysis including review of financial statements, cash flow projections, market trends, and property valuations to support credit decision-making; and (iii) Coordinate with internal partners (Group Risk Management (GRM), Know Your Client (KYC), and Funding and Lending Services) to ensure timely closings.

- Portfolio Transaction Management:  Includes but is not limited to: (i) Review and approve specific drawdown requests; (ii) Develop expertise in assigned portfolio, policies and guidelines, and provide value added advice to internal partners; (iii) Ensure compliance with Bank Policies; and (iv) Participate in team deliverables with respect to regulatory/audit requests.

- Data Integrity: Ensure credit agreement terms are correctly reflected in the Bank’s systems and that all credit documentation is accounted for and reviewed in a timely basis (e.g. credit agreements, amendments, waivers, security documents).

- Other Responsibilities: Completion of ad-hoc projects and other duties (including presenting to key stakeholders) efficiently and effectively in order to support the team’s planned and unplanned demands.

What do you need to succeed?
Must Have's
- Strong academic credentials including completion of a Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Real Estate, or Engineering, mathematics, or any other problem-solving fields.
- You should have one to five years of work experience in a related field, including banking or corporate lending experience, finance and/or risk management, real estate development or investment, or knowledge of structuring and writing of real estate credit proposals, credit processes and policies.
- You are a highly motivated self-starter with keen attention to detail and strong interest in real estate finance and credit.
- You have the ability to read and understand complex legal documents related to real estate transactions, including loan agreements, security documents, and property-related agreements.
- You possess strong credit and analytical skills including the ability to critically assess financial statements, property valuations, market analyses, and other client reports to draw reasoned conclusions and recommend a course of action.
- Your written and verbal communication skills are excellent, with strong negotiation abilities and an ability to manage conflicting demands and viewpoints and multiple stakeholder expectations.
- You work effectively within a team environment and interact well at all levels within a large organization.
- You are able to prioritize, perform well under pressure, and meet time-sensitive deadlines.
- You have strong general PC skills (Excel, Word, and PowerPoint), with proficiency in real estate-specific software or financial modeling tools being a plus.
- Experience with AI models and generative AI tools to enhance analysis and productivity would be highly valuable.

Nice-to-have
- An MBA, CPA, or CFA or other post-graduate degrees with a focus in business, accounting, economics, mathematics, or real estate would be an asset but is not required.

What's in it for you?
We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

- Leaders who support your development through coaching,

- Opportunities to do challenging work and foster strong working relationships with other areas of the bank, including Relationship Managers in Real Estate Corporate Banking, Group Risk Management, Ratings & Monitoring, and Funding and Lending Services, and KYC, amongst others.

The Canadian Risk Solutions Group (RSG) is responsible for providing strategies to hedge interest rate and foreign exchange risk for Canadian-based clients. The team is looking for a Vice President or Director who will primarily focus on the Middle-Market Rates business and assist the broader RSG team.
The candidate will assist in all facets of the business, from managing the marketing and origination of hedging strategies, to pricing and execution of fixed income derivative products.

The level of the position (Director OR Vice President) will be determined based on the candidate's experience and qualifications. Compensation for this role includes a competitive base salary, a variable bonus structure tied to performance, and a comprehensive benefits package. Specific details will be discussed during the interview process and tailored to the candidate's qualifications and the role's requirements.

What will you do?
- Interest rate derivatives coverage of the Canadian Banking Platform including Corporate Client Group, Commercial Financial Services and Wealth Management clients
- Responsible for trade modeling, pricing, execution, booking and related processing of interest rate derivatives and hedging solutions (interest rate swaps, cross-currency swaps, bond forwards, caps/floors, structured rates products, etc.)
- Work closely with the team as a key client contact, providing interest rate risk management advice and education sessions
